obligations.note: The new reopen() method in CaseService.java changes a case from WITHDRAWN to DRAFT and persists it via store.save(), making it a state-changing operation, yet it never calls audit.record(). Every other state-changing method in CaseService (create, edit, submit, approve, override, decline, withdraw, close, addNote, markDocumentReceived, quote, setLegalHold, purgeExpiredNpi) records an audit event; reopen is the sole exception. This directly violates the obligation that every state-changing operation records an audit event with actor, action, target and time.

summary: The change adds a reopen() method to CaseService.java that transitions a withdrawn case back to draft and persists it, but omits the mandatory audit.record() call that every other state-changing operation in the class performs. This is a direct violation of AUD-1, which requires every state-changing operation to record an audit event with actor, action, target, and time. All process obligations (CHG-1 through CHG-7, EXC-1, LAP-1) are satisfied, and the CI suite passed on the final commit, but the sample-based AUD-1 control test does not exercise the new reopen path and cannot compensate for the missing audit call visible in the source. The change must be rejected and the author must add audit.record(actor, Action.EDIT_CASE, caseId, "reopened") before resubmission.
